purpose: Anatomical registry for the Profile-B simulator. Phase 2: five skin layers + correct ordering. Phase 2.5: evidence-anchored schematic draw weights. Phase 2.6: SPECIES-DRIVEN architecture - INDEPENDENT human/mouse/rat anatomy profiles (species_profiles), selected by species with NO silent fallback to human. Defines ONLY the five skin layers, their ordering, per-species schematic draw weights, the scale-level -> visibility mapping, static scenes, labels, and an illustrative palette. Loaded by the app; the code hardcodes NO biological values.

scientific_integrity.ordering_confidence: CONTEXTUAL_ANATOMY - the top-to-bottom ordering (air -> surface -> stratum corneum -> viable epidermis -> dermis -> subcutis) is textbook consensus (OpenStax A&P 5.1 CC BY; StatPearls NBK537325).
scientific_integrity.proportion_basis: Phase 2.5: draw weights are EVIDENCE-ANCHORED (were purely ordinal in Phase 2). Phase 2.6: weights live in INDEPENDENT per-species profiles (species_profiles) - human is evidence-anchored (log10 representative um); mouse/rat use an evidence-supported ORDINAL prominence ladder because per-layer rodent um are not established. NO species copies another's values; NO cross-source averaging. See docs/profile-b-anatomy-scale-validation.md and docs/profile-b-multi-species-anatomy.md.
scientific_integrity.weight_basis: draw_weight = log10(representative_um) for evidence-anchored layers (display-compression, NOT a measurement); subcutis is an ILLUSTRATIVE orientation-only weight (thickness genuinely variable); skin_surface is an interface strip (not a measured layer).
scientific_integrity.why_still_not_to_scale: Even with literature values the dynamic range is ~100x (dermis ~2000 um vs SC ~18 um); a true-to-scale cross-section would render the SC sub-pixel. Weights are therefore log-compressed SCHEMATIC values and the UI must keep the 'schematic - not to scale' caption.
scientific_integrity.rule: Never invent measurements; never average conflicting sources; record disagreement; every value has provenance.

species_scope.statement: Phase 2.6: the anatomy engine is SPECIES-DRIVEN. The active anatomy profile ALWAYS follows the selected species (see species_profiles). Each species profile is INDEPENDENT - no species inherits or copies another's values. 'initial' is only the boot selection (a choice, configurable via app.config anatomy.species and a future Species selector calling app.setSpecies); it is NOT an anatomical fallback. An unknown/unsupported species is an ERROR - there is NO silent fallback to human.
species_scope.context: The Profile-B evidence spans FOUR separate experimental contexts (ex vivo RAT skin permeation; in vitro HaCaT human keratinocytes; in vitro B16BL6 murine melanoma; in vivo C57BL/6 mouse), kept separate per the frozen biological-visualization blueprint. Human, mouse and rat each get their own profile below.

palette.note: ILLUSTRATIVE_COLOR only - restrained, muted, flat fills to DISTINGUISH regions. No gradients, no glow, no concentration/activity encoding.

species_profiles.note: Phase 2.6: INDEPENDENT per-species anatomy DRAWING profiles (supersedes the Phase-2.5 weight_profiles). Each profile is self-contained - NO species inherits another's values. draw_weights are SCHEMATIC drawing weights, NOT physical measurements. Human is EVIDENCE-ANCHORED (log10 representative um). Mouse and rat use an evidence-supported ORDINAL prominence ladder (very_thin 0.7 / thin 1.2 / medium 2.0 / thick 2.8) because per-layer um are NOT established for rodents; magnitudes are schematic, only the ORDERING and relative prominence are claimed. skin_surface (0.3) is a NON-biological interface strip shared as a rendering constant, not a copied measurement. The engine selects a profile by species; the top-level layers[].draw_weight is a structural default equal to the human profile and is NOT used for rodent rendering.

human.weight_basis: EVIDENCE-ANCHORED: draw_weight = log10(representative_um) for SC (18.3)/epidermis (56.6)/dermis (2000 display anchor); subcutis illustrative; skin_surface interface strip.
human.confidence: HIGH - human per-layer um are well established.
references: Sandby-Moller et al. 2003 (PubMed 14690333) - SC + viable epidermis um by site
OpenStax A&P 5.1 (CC BY) - ordering + general thickness
Turkish J Plast Surg 2018 - dermis 1-3 mm range
human.uncertainty: Dermis 1-3 mm (display anchor = flagged range midpoint, not a measurement). Epidermis site-dependent (palms/soles up to ~1 mm); the general non-glabrous value is used.

mouse.weight_basis: ORDINAL prominence ladder (NOT human-derived): mouse skin is thin overall (total ~540 um) with a very thin SC, thin epidermis (~20 um), a medium dermis, and a PRESENT, relatively prominent subcutis owing to the panniculus carnosus (subcutaneous striated muscle).
mouse.confidence: LOW-MEDIUM - ordering + relative prominence supported; per-layer um NOT established.
references: Pharmaceutics 2017;9(3):33 / PMC5620574 (CC BY) - rodent viable epidermis ~20 um, thin SC
Annex JVSAH - C57BL/6 total skin ~540 um
panniculus carnosus (rodent subcutaneous muscle) - standard dermatology histology
mouse.uncertainty: Per-layer SC and dermis um NOT located (~20 um epidermis corroborates 'thin'). Hair-cycle-driven dermal/hypodermal thickness changes are not modelled. Mouse vs rat per-layer distinction is limited to the dermis (rodent skins are otherwise similar).

rat.weight_basis: ORDINAL prominence ladder (NOT human-derived): rat skin is thicker than mouse skin overall; the dermis is the dominant tissue layer (thick) while SC is very thin and epidermis is thin (~20 um). Subcutis present (panniculus carnosus).
rat.confidence: LOW-MEDIUM - ordering + relative prominence supported; per-layer um NOT established.
references: Pharmaceutics 2017;9(3):33 / PMC5620574 (CC BY) - rodent viable epidermis ~20 um
Chen 2012 (Int J Nanomedicine) - Profile-B ex-vivo RAT full-thickness abdominal skin permeation context
panniculus carnosus (rodent subcutaneous muscle) - standard histology
rat.uncertainty: Per-layer SC and dermis um NOT located. Rat abdominal (Chen permeation) vs dorsal site thickness differences are not resolved. The rat-thicker-than-mouse dermis difference is a general, low-confidence claim.

scale_levels.note: Populates the Phase-1 ScaleSystem (L1..L6). depth_window is a [top,bottom] fraction of the full tissue stack (0=surface top, 1=subcutis bottom). emphasized = layers drawn at full opacity; others dimmed. clip = cross-section exposes all layers at overview. UNCHANGED from Phase 2.
